sentences: AI agents can now move money.
But should a chatbot be allowed to press the button?
Left alone, an A I can make things up.
It can be tricked by a single sentence.
A retry can pay the same bill twice.
And two requests can spend the same money.
Fin Guard splits the work into three roles.
Models propose.
Policy decides.
Executors execute.
Let's follow one request. You type: send two thousand pesos to Alex.
Language becomes a typed action. Only three tools exist, so nothing can invent a fourth.
Plain rules check the facts first. No A I is involved.
Then a risk model rates four narrow questions with probabilities. Evidence, never permission.
Policy decides. Every transfer needs your approval, even at ninety nine percent confidence.
One database transaction locks the account, re-checks the balance, and writes two balanced ledger entries.
Every step lands in an audit trail, so the whole story can be replayed.
Not every request takes that path.
A balance check needs no A I at all.
A vague request gets a question instead of a guess.
A suspicious one is held for review.
And if the money isn't there, it stops before any A I is called.
Retries are safe: the same key returns the same result.
Two transfers can't spend the same money.
And if the risk model goes down, the system fails closed instead of skipping the check.
Models propose. Policy decides. Executors execute.
That's Fin Guard: A I you can reason about.
